claims.reason: The abstract and introduction only report that training happened to be stable (no spikes or rollbacks). They never frame stability as a new/novel/first method, and it is absent from the main-contribution list. Not an ARCH/TRAIN novelty claim, so drop it.

claims.quote: We validate our FP8 mixed precision framework with a comparison to BF16 training on top of two baseline models across different scales.
claims.reason: Page 5 lists this as their own contribution ("for the first time, validate" FP8 on an extremely large-scale model), which is a TRAIN precision method. Appendix B compares FP8 vs BF16, but only via loss curves (Figure 10) on smaller proxy MoEs, with no matched benchmark table, so ablation is PARTIAL not YES.
